item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-6eb07dae7fd329be","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In a speech shortly after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Olaf Scholz popularized the term “Zeitenwende” and described the invasion as a fundamental break requiring Germany to revise foreign-policy beliefs and policies; he announced arms deliveries to Ukraine, a significant increase in military spending, and stronger cooperation with like-minded countries.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.4","2B.5","2B.8","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The cited event occurred in 2022, outside the target year; it is contextual evidence for evaluating implementation and effects during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributed to Scholz’s speech and announced program.","limitations":["The source does not establish the 2023 execution, funding, or outcomes of these announcements."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6eb07dae7fd329be","start_unit":11,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"Following Russia’s invasion, German and other Western elites condemned Russia, called for solidarity with Ukraine and protection of territorial integrity, ruled out direct participation by their own forces, and provided Ukraine with arms while imposing sanctions on Russia.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.4","1B.5","2B.5","2B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The source describes the post-invasion policy environment beginning in 2022; it does not isolate Scholz’s 2023 decisions.","ruler_attribution":"Partly attributable to the German government, but the passage describes Western elites collectively and does not identify which measures Scholz personally directed.","limitations":["Collective attribution prevents treating every listed measure as a Scholz-specific act.","The source does not assess legality, civilian effects, or implementation quality."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6eb07dae7fd329be","start_unit":14,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"In the German Longitudinal Election Study panel, support for higher military spending increased by 26 percentage points between December 2021 and May 2022; opposition to recognizing Russia’s annexation of Crimea increased by 25 points; support for a more confrontational Russia policy increased by 16 points; and support for good relations with Putin declined by 23 points.","question_ids":["2B.3","2B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The measurements concern 2021-2022, not 2023; they provide pre-2023 public-opinion context for Scholz’s foreign- and defense-policy agenda.","ruler_attribution":"Contextual public-opinion evidence relevant to the political environment in which Scholz operated, not evidence of a Scholz action.","limitations":["The study does not establish that Scholz caused these opinion changes.","The findings concern attitudes rather than enacted policy or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6eb07dae7fd329be","start_unit":14,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"By October 2022, increased support for higher defense spending and rejection of recognition of Russia’s annexation of Crimea remained durable, while support for good relations with Putin and a more confrontational Russia policy had partly moved back toward pre-invasion levels.","question_ids":["2B.10","8B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence ends in October 2022 and therefore does not directly measure the target year 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Contextual evidence about the durability of public support surrounding Scholz’s policy choices; no direct ruler attribution.","limitations":["No 2023 follow-up is provided.","The source does not link the changes causally to Scholz’s leadership."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6eb07dae7fd329be","start_unit":14,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"The study found no or only minor post-invasion change in core foreign-policy postures, attitudes toward thematically distant issues, or views of Russia, the United States, and China; support for using military force rose only from 18% to 20%, favorable views of the United States rose by 1 point, Atlanticism by 5 points, multilateralism by 4 points, and isolationism declined by 5 points.","question_ids":["2B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"These are 2021-2022 survey comparisons, not direct 2023 evidence.","ruler_attribution":"Contextual evidence indicating that the broader public-attitudinal transformation associated with Scholz’s “Zeitenwende” remained limited during the study period.","limitations":["The source evaluates public opinion, not government implementation or institutional change.","The study’s post-invasion observation period ends in October 2022."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6eb07dae7fd329be","start_unit":15,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"At the individual level, policy attitudes toward issues not directly related to the Ukraine war were largely stable; for China policy, four out of five respondents gave the same answer or differed by only one scale point, while changed views of the United States and core foreign-policy postures showed no clear directional trend.","question_ids":["2B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The individual-level comparisons concern the pre- and post-invasion period through 2022, not 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Contextual evidence about the limits of public support for a broad strategic reorientation under Scholz.","limitations":["No direct evidence of Scholz’s conduct, decisions, or 2023 outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6eb07dae7fd329be","start_unit":15,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"More than one-third of respondents expressed a more negative opinion of Russia after the invasion, compared with 7% who expressed a more positive opinion; views of the United States and China were substantially more stable.","question_ids":["2B.3","2B.10"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The evidence concerns changes through 2022 and is not a 2023 measurement.","ruler_attribution":"Contextual public-opinion evidence relevant to the external environment for Scholz’s Russia policy.","limitations":["The result does not show that Scholz caused the change or that it translated into durable policy support."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6eb07dae7fd329be","start_unit":16,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"The study found no meaningful subgroup-level turning point: foreign-policy postures remained highly stable across subgroups, and differences in policy-attitude change were generally small; changes were somewhat greater among mainstream-party supporters and politically interested citizens.","question_ids":["2B.10","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The subgroup analysis covers the invasion-related period through 2022, not 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Contextual evidence about the breadth and limits of the public mandate for Scholz’s foreign-policy shift.","limitations":["This is not evidence of a Scholz decision or administrative performance."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6eb07dae7fd329be","start_unit":17,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"The authors conclude that opinion changes were confined to war-related policy issues such as military spending and a more confrontational Russia policy; core postures and attitudes toward unrelated issues and actors did not change, so there was insufficient evidence of a turning point in German public opinion.","question_ids":["2B.10","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The conclusion is based on data through October 2022, before the target year.","ruler_attribution":"Indirectly relevant to Scholz’s claimed “Zeitenwende”; the authors assess public opinion rather than Scholz’s institutional performance.","limitations":["The article explicitly states that its post-invasion data cover only about eight months and cannot settle long-term durability.","It does not evaluate 2023 policy implementation."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied source is a scholarly study of German public opinion, with most evidence covering 2021-2022 rather than Olaf Scholz’s 2023 actions.","The source contains little direct evidence about domestic safety, democratic institutions, social welfare, integrity, or 2023 administrative implementation."]}
